edges.description: Impaired stimulated triglyceride breakdown was associated with excess adipose triglyceride storage, but causality and the intervening molecular step were not directly demonstrated.
edges.source: Post-cAMP Failure of Isoprenaline-Stimulated Adipocyte Lipolysis

edges.description: All three members assigned to the preserved-cAMP type II pattern were described as generalized obese, but whether the measured lipolytic defect caused their obesity is unresolved.

nodes.description: Excess adipose triglyceride storage was reported in the provisional historical disease group. For type II, its causal dependence on the ex vivo isoprenaline-response defect remains plausible but unproven, particularly because fasting-mediated lipid mobilization was retained.

evidence.snippet: Four patients are described with metabolic defects on the paths of triglyceride breakdown associated with excessive storage of triglyceride in adipose tissue.

nodes.description: Generalized obesity was present in the three related patients assigned to the type II biochemical pattern. The very small historical kindred does not define penetrance, severity distribution, or specificity relative to common obesity.

evidence.snippet: In three other generalized obese patients of a kindred, isoprenaline (10−5M) stimulated the activity of adenyl cyclase in subcutaneous adipose tissue as judged by normal increments in tissue levels of cyclic-AMP but this failed to activate the triglyceride lipase; seen as a reduced output of glycerol compared to obese controls (P < 0.01).

nodes.description: Subcutaneous adipose tissue from the reported type II kindred increased cyclic AMP after isoprenaline but released abnormally little glycerol. The historical authors placed the candidate lesion somewhere downstream of adenylate cyclase and cyclic AMP, but neither the affected protein nor the precise activation or lipase step was established.

evidence.reference_title: Triglyceride storage disease: a disorder of lipolysis in adipose tissue in two patients.
evidence.snippet: An obese patient was studied whose adipose tissue showed a significant reduction in release of glycerol (P < 0.05) when stimulated by isoprenaline despite normal rises in tissue levels of cyclic-AMP.
